title: JavaScript linting, formatting, and source maps
concepts: Lint rules identify suspicious or invalid patterns
Formatting tools make layout deterministic without changing intended behavior
TypeScript linting needs parser and project-aware rule integration
Source maps map generated locations back to authored sources
Linting, formatting, and type checking solve different problems

inventory.title: Current JavaScript and TypeScript lint/format tools
Core lint configuration and rule controls

items: Flat config became the default configuration system; eslintrc remained temporarily available with migration guidance.
The eslintrc configuration system was removed; flat config is the only supported format. ESLint v10.15.0 was released 2026-11-13 in this snapshot.

The migration guide documents breaking changes that affect Node.js support, config lookup, rule behavior, and APIs; consult the version-specific guide when upgrading rather than assuming the config-format change is the only change.
Import organization moved into assist.actions.source.organizeImports; v1 configuration and sorting assumptions need migration.
The Source Map v3 data format was specified as an Ecma standard; the map version field remains the integer 3.

sourceSnapshot.authority: Official ESLint, typescript-eslint, Prettier, Biome, and ECMA-426 documentation

accuracyFacts: ESLint flat config became the default in ESLint 9.0.0; ESLint 10.0.0 removed the legacy eslintrc configuration system entirely. Current 10.x examples should use only flat config; older migration notes must distinguish when legacy config was still available.

In flat config, a config object with only ignores establishes global ignores; ignores combined with other properties applies locally to that config object. globalIgnores is the explicit helper for global ignore patterns in current ESLint documentation.
ESLint severity values off, warn, and error correspond to disabled, warning, and error reporting. They are lint outcomes, not runtime JavaScript exceptions.

typescript-eslint typed rules require TypeScript type information and usually cost more time. The current recommended projectService option uses the nearest TypeScript project; files outside its project need deliberate configuration or should not receive typed rules.

ESLint is a lint engine and formatter, Prettier is an opinionated formatter, and Biome provides formatter, linter, and assist actions. Their rule sets and formatting are not interchangeable; choose one formatting authority to avoid conflicting rewrites.

Prettier resolves project configuration from the formatted file's directory upward and intentionally has no global configuration. Its ignore file and plugins affect which files and syntaxes are formatted.
Biome v2 organizes imports through the assist source action configuration; the older top-level organizeImports configuration was migrated. Do not teach the v1 configuration shape as current.
ECMA-426 defines the current source map format and fixes the map version field to integer 3. The version field is not a tool/package version and does not identify the edition of the standard.

Source maps use generated/source/name tables and Base64 VLQ mappings; JavaScript and CSS generated columns are zero-based UTF-16 code-unit offsets. Index maps use non-overlapping ordered sections with generated offsets.

sourcesContent is optional original source text and may expose source code when published. ignoreList marks source indices that developer tools may treat as third-party code; it does not change execution.

A source map can be linked by a sourceMappingURL annotation or HTTP sourcemap header; the header takes precedence when both are present under ECMA-426. Inline/external/hidden describe delivery or bundler conventions, not separate mapping semantics.

A source map improves debugging and stack deobfuscation but does not guarantee perfect source-level stepping; transform chains, missing mappings, mismatched deployed artifacts, or invalid source origins can reduce accuracy.
The ESLint 10 migration has changes beyond removing eslintrc; the version-specific migration guide must be followed for runtime support, config lookup, and other breaking changes.
scopeExclusions: Exhaustive per-rule catalogs for individual lint plugins
